evidence: src/domain/errors.ts: DomainError is the shared base for ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError, and all entities use it.
src/domain/task.ts: TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus and isTaskStatus are defined once and reused by Task.create and by TaskFilter.status in repositories.ts.
src/domain/project.ts, user.ts and task.ts all follow the same pattern: private constructor, static create(props) that validates and throws ValidationError, and toJSON().

src/domain/repositories.ts: UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository are typed against the domain entities. IdGenerator and Clock are ports too, but they sit in a file named for repositories (minor naming issue).

Project.create, User.create and Task.create each repeat the 'trim then reject empty' check as separate per-entity invariants with their own messages, so this is not one shared rule duplicated out of its proper home.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain is one cohesive domain-model unit. It holds the entities (Project, Task, User), their shared error hierarchy (DomainError and its subclasses) and the ports the application layer needs (repositories plus IdGenerator and Clock). The files use their abstractions consistently. Each entity has a private constructor and a static create factory that validates input and throws ValidationError. The task status rule is defined once (TASK_STATUSES, TaskStatus, isTaskStatus) and reused by Task.create and by TaskFilter in repositories.ts. All errors come from errors.ts; no file throws a bare Error or defines its own error class. Project.create, User.create and Task.create each repeat the same 'trim and reject empty' check. These are separate per-entity invariants with entity-specific messages, not one rule copied out of its proper home. A small naming issue: IdGenerator and Clock live in repositories.ts even though they are not repositories. They are still domain ports and fit the module's boundary. None of these rise to a split concern, a duplicated invariant or a bypassed abstraction.
